arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Andrew Pincus argued the statute covers all offenses involving cocaine base, not just crack.
Saharsky argued that freebase, coca paste, and crack are chemically identical and smokeable.
Justice Roberts noted the statute refers to a mixture containing cocaine base.
Justice Scalia questioned whether the term crack excludes substances not made in a specific manner.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests the scope of a federal drug statute. the side that brought the case argues the law covers all smokeable cocaine base. The government argues the law targets only rock-hard crack.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants the Court to apply the mandatory minimum penalty to all smokeable cocaine base forms.
The government wants the Court to limit the mandatory minimum penalty to rock-hard crack cocaine only.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues that Congress did not limit the statute to one specific form of cocaine base.
The government argues that the statute specifically targets substances with the characteristics of crack cocaine.
